svg.aria-label: The daemon: 11 states and 20 changes, 15 fired by a clock and 5 by a fact. Each change is an arrow; its table follows.
svg.title: The daemon: 11 states and 20 changes, 15 fired by a clock and 5 by a fact. Each change is an arrow; its table follows.

g.title: DM1, none to starting, fired by a fact: a hook finds no daemon and starts `rerail daemon start` detached; or a person runs it

DM2, starting to starting, fired by a clock: the autostart claim: a file with a 5 s lease, renewed each second for at most 45 s; a claim not renewed is taken for abandoned Timers: A110 D1 D33. Fact that could fire it: An OS lock the launcher holds for its life: the system frees it however the launcher ends. It becomes a fact.

DM3, starting to starting, fired by a clock: waiting for the start lock: the lock file is tried every 50 ms for up to 15 s Timers: A107 B005 B006 C27. Fact that could fire it: A blocking OS lock wait (flock without LOCK_NB; LockFileEx without LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY), served in arrival order. It becomes a fact.

DM4, starting to starting, fired by a clock: the home lock says a daemon holds the home but daemon.json is missing: polled every 100 ms for up to 15 s, then an error Timers: A108. Fact that could fire it: The home lock's holder record names the daemon: act on it, or watch the home folder for daemon.json. It becomes a fact.
DM5, starting to launched, fired by a fact: the launcher spawns the daemon after the SQLite binding check (no limit on that check)

DM6, launched to none, fired by a clock: a second daemon for the same home tries the home lock every 50 ms for 1 s, then stops Timers: B007 B008 D41. Fact that could fire it: The predecessor's exit (its process handle) and a blocking wait on the home lock. It becomes a fact.

DM7, launched to alive, fired by a clock: the daemon listens and writes daemon.json; the launcher sees it by reading daemon.json and /healthz every 100 ms, up to 15 s Timers: A109 A205 A206 A207 B220 B221 B222 D5 D59. Fact that could fire it: A ready line the daemon writes on a pipe the launcher passed it once it listens; the pipe's end is its exit. It a fact, one bound left.

DM8, launched to none, fired by a clock: the daemon died at start: on Windows the launcher reads its exit code every 100 ms Timers: C26 C52. Fact that could fire it: A wait registered on the kept process handle (RegisterWaitForSingleObject); a pidfd or kqueue NOTE_EXIT elsewhere. It becomes a fact.

DM9, alive to busy, fired by a clock: the event loop is held by work (an audit, a collection, a long write); no code marks it: a client sees it only as a probe unanswered within 2 s Timers: A104 A106. Fact that could fire it: None for the first wait: nothing tells a daemon that answers in 3 s from one that never will. It stays.

DM10, busy to not answering, fired by a clock: a hook gives up 12 s after it arrived (2 s probe, then a second probe with the rest) and loses its event Timers: A101 A102 A222 D58. Fact that could fire it: An earlier event the daemon has left untaken: every hook after the first of a silence can answer at once and journal its event. It becomes a fact.

DM11, alive to taken for gone, fired by a clock: on Windows a proof that waited out Node's 30 s pipe connect reads 'gone', and the lookup deletes the live daemon's daemon.json Timers: A105. Fact that could fire it: The home daemon lock (homeDaemonRuns): a daemon that holds it is alive. It becomes a fact.

DM12, alive to alive, fired by a clock: the daemon checks every 1 s that daemon.json still holds its record and writes it back Timers: A204 D30 D31. Fact that could fire it: A watch on the home folder. It becomes a fact.
DM13, alive to stopping, fired by a fact: SIGTERM or SIGINT (macOS, Linux); POST /native/shutdown on Windows

DM14, alive to stopping, fired by a clock: on Windows a stop request not answered in 2 s turns into a kill, cutting the requests in flight Timers: A113. Fact that could fire it: The request's answer, given a clean shutdown its time; the exit itself by the process handle. It becomes a fact.

DM15, stopping to stopping, fired by a clock: the close drains: looks for stalled requests every 1 s, waits 2 s for a Merge Assist pass, 0.5 s for hook commands, up to 5 s for the Windows watch's cancelled reads Timers: A117 A605 A609 C24 D15 D16 D17 D18 D19 D20 D21 D22 D23. Fact that could fire it: Each wait already ends on its event; the clocks bound a party that never answers. Merge Assist's stop can wait for the hook commands only. It a fact, one bound left.

DM16, stopping to none, fired by a clock: `rerail daemon stop` sees the exit by a 100 ms poll; at 10 s it sends SIGKILL and waits 5 s more Timers: A111 A112. Fact that could fire it: The exit by the process handle (pidfd, kqueue NOTE_EXIT, WaitForSingleObject); the kill at 10 s stays for a daemon that ignores its stop. It a fact, one bound left.

DM17, alive to restarting, fired by a clock: the heap is read every 30 s; past 80% of its limit, and not within 10 min of start, the daemon relaunches itself Timers: A208 A209. Fact that could fire it: Node's 'gc' performance entry after each full collection. It becomes a fact.
DM18, alive to replaced at an update, fired by a fact: `rerail update` stops the daemon, installs and starts the new version; limits fire only when a step hangs
DM19, alive to suspended by the system, fired by a fact: the machine sleeps; no Rerail code runs and none marks it

DM20, suspended by the system to alive, fired by a clock: at resume every age measured on the wall clock (Date.now, SystemTime) counts the sleep as quiet time: a session whose last event is over 30 min old closes at the next 60 s sweep and its next tool call waits for the reopen; a native session reads expired until its host's next request, and a sweep that comes first closes it; content-store leases read expired until the next renewal Timers: A118 A211 C08 C11 C13. Fact that could fire it: No age at all: an owner's end as the fact (the agent's exit, the host's connection, the workspace's process). The systems' resume notices (logind PrepareForSleep, NSWorkspaceDidWakeNotification, WM_POWERBROADCAST) would only patch the ages. It a fact, one bound left.
